parts.title: Can a WOOL Scarf Keep Ice Cream COLD? The Great Ice Cream Rescue | P3 to P4 Science
parts.description:
The class party starts in 20 minutes. The ice cream is still at the mama shop. It is 33 degrees outside. Pip has three plans: run faster, fan it, or wrap it in his WOOL scarf. Pick the fix that saves the ice cream, then watch every plan get tested, mistakes and all, in our Primary 3 finale and the very first taste of Primary 4 Science.

In this video:
• The problem: ice cream vs the Singapore sun
• Pick the fix: run, fan, or wool?
• Fix 1: Pip runs (and runs out of puff). Is the cold going into his tummy?
• Fix 2: the fan, in slow motion. Look closer: 33 °C vs minus 18 °C
• Fix 3: wool?! Shrink down into the scarf's trapped air
• A fair test: no wrapper, a plastic bag, or wool?
• A magnet to the rescue at the drain
• The words that earn marks, and see you in Primary 4!
• Stay for the blooper after the end!

Key words: hotter to colder, poor conductor of heat, fair test.
The words that earn marks: Heat flows from a hotter place to a colder place. Wool is a poor conductor of heat. It slows down the heat flowing from the warmer surroundings to the ice cream.

For parents: this is a story, not a lecture. Children pick a fix with their fingers before each idea is tested, so they think before they are told. It finishes Primary 3 (fair tests, magnets) and opens Primary 4 Heat (P4 Chapters 6 and 7: heat flows from hotter to colder; good and poor conductors of heat; trapped air). A common mistake it fixes: "the cold goes into my hand". Nothing cold flows: heat flows out of the warmer thing into the colder one. Also fits US NGSS 4-PS3-2 (Grade 4).
Try it at home (with an adult): put two ice cubes on two saucers, wrap one in a wool sock, and check both after 15 minutes. Change only the wrapper, keep everything else the same.

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies!
